newsitem.title: USA: Groups sue to block Chugach timber sale.
newsitem.headline: Groups sue to block Chugach timber sale.

text.p: A coalition of environmental groups Wednesday filed a lawsuit in U.S. District Court to block an upcoming timber sale in Alaska's Chugach National Forest.

The groups said they want to stop the Moose Pass Salvage Sale, the first in a series intended to clear so-called "salvage" timber -- beetle-infested or otherwide dead or dying trees -- from the forest.

In their lawsuit against the U.S. Forest Service, they said the agency failed to consider the cumulative effects of the Moose Pass sale and other timber sales in the national forest on Alaska's Kenai Peninsula.
Plaintiffs include the Anchorage chapter of the Audubon Society, the Sierra Club Legal Defense Fund and several local and state groups.

The Moose Pass sale encompasses 2,259 acres and involves more than 12 miles of new roads on the southern tip of Alaska's Kenai Peninsula. The sale site is about 25 miles north of Seward, a popular tourist destination and fishing port.
The four timber sales planned for the coming year would put on the market nearly as much Chugach timber as had been offered for logging over the past decade, the groups said.
The logging and road-building would harm the area's wildlife and recreational qualities, the environmentalists said.
